report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is not simply false, but it is **not established strongly enough to call acupuncture a proven treatment** for depression during pregnancy.

The principal direct evidence is a 2010 randomized trial of 150 pregnant people with major depression. Participants received depression-specific acupuncture, nonspecific (“control”) acupuncture, or massage for eight weeks. The reported response rate was higher with depression-specific acupuncture (about 63%) than with control acupuncture (37.5%) or massage (50%). Outcomes were assessed by masked raters, which is a strength. However, this was one modest-sized, short-term study; it did not compare acupuncture with a credible inert sham procedure, psychotherapy, or usual clinical care, and the massage/control interventions can neither fully blind participants nor eliminate expectancy and attention effects.  
https://journals.lww.com/greenjournal/fulltext/10.1097/aog.0b013e3181cc0816~acupuncture-for-depression-during-pregnancy-a-randomized

An earlier pilot trial was smaller and explicitly cautioned that its relatively homogeneous sample limited generalizability.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15546651/

More broadly, Cochrane’s review of acupuncture for depression (not limited to pregnancy) included 64 randomized trials/7,104 participants but highlights the difficulties of the evidence base; acupuncture studies often vary substantially and sham-controlled evidence is especially important for separating specific needling effects from placebo/contextual effects.  
https://www.cochrane.org/CD004046/DEPRESSN_acupuncture-depression

Thus, the defensible view is: **there is preliminary, trial-based evidence of symptom improvement, but insufficient replicated, high-quality pregnancy-specific evidence to conclude that acupuncture reliably reduces antenatal depression symptoms.** It should not replace evidence-based assessment and treatment (especially psychotherapy and, when indicated, medication decisions made with an obstetric and mental-health clinician).
